MyFitnessPal review: costs, food tracking, meal-planning features and limitations

A research-based review covering everyday use, paid features and where the app may fall short.

By Nutrition.Fitness · 15 September 2026 · 4 min read

The short answer

MyFitnessPal is a sensible shortlist option for food logging, with a free tier and paid tools. Premium+ also offers UK meal planning, although its supermarket-app integration is not currently a UK feature. We could not verify one current GBP checkout price. This research-based review explains what to check before paying and when keeping the free version makes more sense.

MyFitnessPal is worth considering if you want to understand and record what you eat. Start with its free version if basic logging meets your needs. Pay only when a specific paid feature makes your routine easier. Its Premium+ plan also includes meal planning, so describing it as merely a calorie counter would be unfair.

This is a research-based review, not hands-on testing. We checked official product information on 15 September 2026. Nutrition.Fitness is developing NUFI, a competing programme and meal-planning system, so we have a commercial interest. That does not make switching to us the right answer for everyone.

What are you actually buying?

OptionMain reason to consider itQuestion to ask yourself
FreeBasic food loggingDoes recording my usual meals already give me enough useful information?
PremiumAdditional logging tools and nutrition controlsWhich paid tool would I genuinely use?
Premium+Premium features plus meal planningDo I need help choosing meals as well as recording them?

The official free-plan guide and Premium+ feature list describe these options. Premium tools include barcode, photo and voice logging, customised goals and an advertising-free experience.

How much does it cost in the UK?

We could not reliably verify a single current GBP checkout price across UK purchase routes. MyFitnessPal's public pages can show other currencies, and paid options vary by plan and billing route. We will not turn a US dollar price into a supposed UK price. See the official plan selector, set your correct region and check the payment screen.

Record the amount charged today, the subscription tier, whether it covers one month or one year, and the renewal amount. An annual equivalent is not a monthly instalment. If an annual option hypothetically costs £60 and monthly costs £10, six monthly payments equal the annual fee. Those are illustrative numbers, not MyFitnessPal prices. Paying annually only helps if you want the access for long enough.

Does its meal planner work for UK buyers?

MyFitnessPal says Meal Planner is available to UK Premium+ subscribers using a supported English-language mobile app. It is not available on its website. Its grocery-app integration is currently restricted to the US and Canada, so UK buyers should not expect a supermarket basket to populate automatically. These distinctions appear in the official Meal Planner guide.

For a busy household, the practical test is whether the suggested meals fit your actual shopping and cooking. A recipe that needs six ingredients you never use may add work. Try a familiar week: one late finish, one leftover night and one meal everybody already likes. Could the plan cope without you rebuilding it?

What we would check before upgrading

  • Find three packaged foods you buy regularly and check serving sizes against their labels.
  • Record one homemade meal. Notice whether saving and reusing it feels manageable.
  • Check the exact device integration you need rather than assuming every smartwatch behaves alike.
  • Check which paid feature removes a real inconvenience. A longer feature list is not automatically better value.
  • Ask whether logging leaves you informed or increasingly preoccupied with food.

These are suggested checks, not tests we have performed. We cannot give a credible score for speed, accuracy or ease of use from product pages alone. If tracking becomes upsetting or compulsive, step back and consider a meal routine without calorie logging; seek appropriate professional support if that distress persists.

Who should choose something else?

If your main need is someone watching your exercise technique or adapting sessions around an injury, confirm that service with a suitably qualified professional. A food diary cannot substitute for it. If you already cook happily and only need basic information, the free version may be sufficient. If your existing MyFitnessPal routine works, familiarity is a valid reason to keep it.

Before a paid trial or subscription, read MyFitnessPal's cancellation instructions for the platform taking your payment. Deleting an app and cancelling a subscription are different actions.

Compare NUFI's listed offer only if you want programmes and meal planning together. Our current site is a preview with login and payment not connected. Your next question is simple: do you need help recording food, deciding what to cook, or deciding how to train?

Sources and checks

Information checked on 15 September 2026. Prices, availability and subscriptions can change; check the linked provider before paying.
